transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM); Liam Carter (Orion Head of ML), Priya Rao (Platform), Noah Kim (CTO), Sara Mendes (Security)

Summary: quick POC scoping to align on workload characterization, QPS, concurrency, input/output token distribution, benchmark plan and timeline. Customer wants latency p95 < 150ms for single-turn auth flows and production-like throughput in a 2-week dedicated trial.

Topics: success criteria, traffic modeling, sample artifacts, infra/network constraints, security docs, benchmark schedule.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros - i'm jenna redwood ae, marco our se will run the workload modeling.
[00:22] Liam Carter: hi all, liam here, head of ml at orion payments. we run a few LLM-driven features—auth-fraud detection, realtime dispute summarization, and the new user onboarding assistant.
[00:35] Marco Silva: great, quick question up front, are we scoping the POC around the fraud detection realtime path or the onboarding assistant, both have different token and latency profiles?
[00:46] Noah Kim: primarily fraud detection realtime for this POC, onboarding later. fraud path is single-turn inference per transaction, need low p95 latency.
[00:58] Priya Rao: to add, we have batch reranking jobs at night but not part of the low-latency requirement.
[01:10] Marco Silva: got it. can you share current load numbers at a high level? qps / concurrency / token sizes?
[01:22] Liam Carter: our prod average is around 120 QPS for the fraud endpoint, with peaks up to 350 qps during promo spikes. concurrency for long running sessions is low, maybe 8-12, but short-lived concurrent requests hit 220-300 during peaks.
[01:46] Jenna Park: ok that's helpful. what about tokens per request—input and expected output?
[01:52] Liam Carter: typical input median is ~65 tokens (transaction context + merchant history snippet), output is terse, median 28 tokens—most responses are 10-60 tokens. tail out to 200 tokens in complex cases but rare.
[02:10] Marco Silva: that distribution maps to a short sequence workload, good for batching and KV/prefix cache. for the POC we usually model 3 profiles: baseline (avg 120 qps), peak (350 qps) and stress (500 qps synthetic) to ensure headroom.
[02:32] Priya Rao: what hardware are you recommending for the trial? we run in GCP and can run dedicated GPUs or private if needed.
[02:40] Marco Silva: for realtime low-latency single-turn models we recommend a Dedicated setup on A100/H100 class. for this token profile, 2x A100-equivalent workers should reproduce 120-350 qps with good p95, but we'll run a benchmark to tune batch sizes and quantization.
[02:57] Sara Mendes: from security, we need VPC peering, SAML SSO for the console, KMS integration and SOC2 docs. can you send the papers?
[03:10] Jenna Park: absolutely, we'll send SOC2 type II, security whitepaper and network topology. we can support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments too.
[03:22] Liam Carter: success criteria—what do you see as a typical POC success checklist?
[03:28] Aisha Khan: we usually define 3 buckets: functional correctness (model quality within delta vs current baseline), performance (latency p95 <150ms and throughput targets), and ops/security (networking, audit logs and SSO). also cost/per-token estimates for the projected load.
[03:48] Marco Silva: to add, we'll capture regression tests using your prompt set and do an eval run to measure precision/recall vs your labeled incidents.
[03:58] Noah Kim: what's the expected time to run the benchmark? we're hoping to have results within a week of data handoff.
[04:05] Marco Silva: typically once we get the sample traffic (72h), we can configure and run benchmarks within 48-72 hours; then a day to analyze. so 5 business days end-to-end if nothing blocks.
[04:18] Priya Rao: network: can we avoid opening inbound rules? we prefer outbound-only peering.
[04:25] Jenna Park: that's fine; we support outbound-only peering for Dedicated as long as egress routes are allowed. we'll include our network checklist.
[04:36] Liam Carter: cost is a factor. can you ballpark unit economics for this load?
[04:40] Marco Silva: rough back-of-the-envelope: with batching and prefix caching we often reduce per-token cost by 2-3x vs naive single-request runs. For your median sizes we'd estimate %cost per 1M tokens roughly comparable to hosted pricing on standard models but dedicated pricing depends on reserved capacity. we'll send a detailed cost model in the spreadsheet.
[04:59] Priya Rao: curious about quantization—would an int8 path degrade quality?
[05:04] Marco Silva: int8/4-bit quantization often has small quality impact on short-sequence classification tasks; we'll do side-by-side quality eval with your prompt set. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles automatically based on evals.
[05:20] Jenna Park: let's talk measurements—what are your required SLOs and what metrics should we collect in the POC?
[05:28] Noah Kim: p95 latency < 150ms, p99 < 350ms ideally, < 2% false positives increase vs current model, and we need audit logs for all requests for compliance.
[05:40] Marco Silva: we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, cpu/gpu utilization, batching efficiency, cache hit rates, and token counts per request. we'll also collect end-to-end wall clock per request so you can compare to current infra.
[05:55] Liam Carter: do you support multi-model routing? we sometimes fall back to a smaller cheaper model when the primary is overloaded.
[06:02] Marco Silva: yes. Smart routing can fallback from a higher-cost model to a cheaper variant with graceful degradation; routing policies can be by latency, cost or region. we'll demo that in the benchmark if you want.
[06:15] Priya Rao: great. sample artifacts—what format do you need for traffic?
[06:20] Jenna Park: a request log CSV or ndjson with timestamp, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens (if available), sample input text (anonymized), and a label for whether a human was in the loop.
[06:34] Liam Carter: we can produce an ndjson with masked PII, we'll get it to you by Thursday.
[06:40] Marco Silva: perfect. for workload modeling we'll ask you to mark a few sessions that represent the heavy-tail cases so we can emulate those as well.
[06:50] Aisha Khan: timeline suggestion: traffic by 6/17, Redwood config and bench by 6/21, trial Dedicated capacity provisioned 6/22, 2-week run 6/22-7/06, security signoff in parallel. does that align?
[07:05] Noah Kim: that aligns but security will need the SOC2 and the network checklist earlier.
[07:11] Sara Mendes: yes, send docs asap, and we may require an MOU before peering.
[07:17] Jenna Park: we'll include a standard MOU template with the network docs.
[07:24] Liam Carter: are you able to run a synthetic stress test to 500 qps and check tail latency? that's a hard requirement for us in peak events.
[07:33] Marco Silva: yes we will run three phases: baseline, peak, stress. stress will run synthetic at 500 qps for 10 minutes to exercise autoscaling/fallback. we'll also instrument KV cache to show how cache hit rate reduces tokens sent to the model.
[07:50] Priya Rao: on caching, do you do prefix caching per session? we have repeated merchant metadata in many calls.
[07:56] Marco Silva: yes, prefix/KV cache is supported; for repeated merchant contexts it can be a big win—reducing input tokens and latency. we'll show savings in the bench spreadsheet.
[08:08] Liam Carter: a nit—how do you handle concurrent requests that update the KV cache? race conditions?
[08:14] Marco Silva: cache updates are append-only per session key and we have consistency windows; for your real-time fraud flow most entries are read-heavy so it's safe. we can discuss specifics with your infra team.
[08:27] Noah Kim: logging and audit—will we get request-level logs with token counts and model version?
[08:33] Jenna Park: yes, the console exposes per-request logs, model version, route tags and cost breakdown. we can push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder.
[08:45] Sara Mendes: does that include masked content for PII?
[08:48] Marco Silva: logs can be configured to mask or omit content fields; we can also store full transcripts in a customer-controlled S3 if needed and leave only metadata in Redwood logs.
[09:00] Liam Carter: what about compliance for EU data residency? some of our merchant data must not leave region.
[09:06] Jenna Park: we support region pinning and private deployments; Dedicated can be in a specific region or Private for full on-prem if required. we'll discuss options after we see your sample traffic.
[09:18] Aisha Khan: i'll send the POC success template—fields include quality delta thresholds, latency SLOs, operational criteria, and sign-off owners.
[09:27] Priya Rao: who will own the benchmark config?
[09:30] Marco Silva: se team will own the config with support from your platform eng, we'll share the config as a repo snippet and the bench spreadsheet.
[09:38] Liam Carter: any recommended open models or do you advise bringing our own fine-tuned model?
[09:44] Marco Silva: if you have a tuned model we can serve it; otherwise we'll use a Redwood-verified open model with similar architecture to give you a baseline. serving your fine-tune often gives the best quality comparison.
[09:58] Noah Kim: ok, so to recap success criteria: p95 <150ms, p99 <350ms, quality delta <2% false pos, audit logs enabled, and ops signoff. timeline: traffic 6/17, bench 6/21, trial 6/22-7/06.
[10:13] Jenna Park: that's the plan. we'll send action items and docs after this call.
[10:18] (cross talk) Marco Silva: i'll capture the traffic shape assumptions: avg 120 qps, peak 350 qps, stress 500 qps synthetic; median input 65 tokens, median output 28 tokens, tail up to 200.
[10:34] Priya Rao: what about concurrency, are you modeling request bursts?
[10:37] Marco Silva: yes bursts modeled as poisson arrivals with short spikes sustained for 5-15 minutes for promo events; that will exercise autoscaler and routing fallback.
[10:49] Liam Carter: will you provide a cost estimate showing cost at baseline vs peak for 1M requests per day?
[10:54] Marco Silva: yes we'll provide a cost model with token-level costs and Dedicated amortized cost; also show savings from batching and caching.
[11:05] Sara Mendes: final question—are any third-party partners involved in this POC?
[11:09] Jenna Park: not required, but we occasionally pull infra partners for network setup. we'll coordinate if needed.
[11:18] Noah Kim: good. any blockers from our side?
[11:20] Liam Carter: none besides getting the sample logs and security docs signed MOU.
[11:25] Jenna Park: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and scheduling links.
[11:31] Marco Silva: thanks, we'll prep the benchmark config.
[11:35] Aisha Khan: i'll open a POC Jira and add owners.
[11:38] (meeting end)

Notes: transcript shows periodic timestamps through the first 11 minutes (call recorded ~54 minutes total). remainder of the call covered detailed bench config, repo links, and a short demo of routing UI which is captured in the action items. Some transcription noise (crosstalk, slight mis-attributions) present as typical Fireflies export.
